PAGE_3:
ESSENTIAL BUSINESS WRITING SKILLS – ACTION GUIDE 
  IAPWE Professional Development Series 3  How to Use Your Action Guide  You’ll get the best results from any course you participate in by completing the Action Steps at the end of each module. They will help you apply what you learn directly to your business and your life, maximizing the investment you’re making.  Use the following Action Guide to record your answers, insights, and other notes for the Action Steps, which are outlined in your Course Book. You’ll want to refer to each module’s content as you complete the related steps.  While we have left space in the guide for each action step, you may feel more comfortable using a separate notebook or digital application for your work. Use whatever method you feel most comfortable with and don’t feel constrained to using the space in the Action Guide alone.  In addition, your course may have other Action Sheets, such as spreadsheets or planning templates, which are separate from the guide. Look out for those with your other course materials.  Finally, you don’t have to complete all the steps at once. Instead, try setting a specific time on your calendar to work on them. And don’t feel that you have to get it right the first time. Learning is a process that happens as you apply your new skills and knowledge. You’ll want to return periodically to your Action Guide and both remind yourself of the work you’ve achieved and edit your answers as you see their impact.   Have fun with it and enjoy the progress and successes that will happen as a result of your work!

  IAPWE Professional Development Series 8 Lesson 2: Pick the Appropriate Tone 1. Formal and Informal Language Exercise: Below are two emails that cover similar content, but are different in the way they are written. Study them and identify their differences. Email 1 Hey Michelle!  Just heard about your promotion. Congrats! Now you can hopefully get that fancy new car you’ve been eyeing 😊 Fyi, I’m busy working on the revisions you asked for on that proposal doc. Should be ready soon. Any urgency? See you later. Adam  Email 2 Dear Michelle, Thank you for sending me the proposal document for Easynet Incorporated for review. I am pleased to inform you that we have begun work on the revision and that we fully expect to be able to return it to you by the end of the week. In our earlier discussions, you mentioned that you were currently experiencing some issues with deadlines. To help facilitate this, there is a possibility that we could send you the revised version before the agreed deadline of Friday. If you would like us to do this, please let me know as soon as possible and I will take the necessary steps to ensure that it is completed and returned to you on Thursday. Should this not be necessary, we will make sure that you receive the document on Friday.

PAGE_9:
ESSENTIAL BUSINESS WRITING SKILLS – ACTION GUIDE 
  IAPWE Professional Development Series 9 Finally, I understand from your post that you have recently been promoted. I would like to take this opportunity to congratulate you and to wish you every success in your new position. I look forward to hearing from you if you decide the report is needed on Thursday. Best regards, Adam Nelson-Tucker  What differences do you notice between the two emails? What relationship do you think these people have? Look at tone, voice, content, and any other aspects you consider important.

  IAPWE Professional Development Series 11 Lesson 3: Organize Your Thoughts 1. Logical Flow Exercise: Read the piece of following text which forms the first part of an internal report in a small company. Make any changes you think are necessary to the flow of information. You want to make sure that the text moves logically from one point to another. “We recently went to hardware stores, bathroom fixture stores, and pharmacies and found five competitive products. To avoid any risk of breaches of patent, we paid particular attention to products sufficiently different from ours but which try to solve the same problem. This was part of a recent survey to find any competitive products on the market that were similar to our proposed designs for easily operated taps for people with arthritis. The fourth product does claim to solve the design problem, but it does so from a different angle. Three of these help people to operate indoor house taps but do not address the issue of taps in the yard. The fifth competitive product also aims to provide ease of operation but is too similar to our design C to be considered.”
